faqs.a:
(a)
To facilitate the progress of the hearing, and to ensure fairness, the parties will
               make a good faith effort to exchange information concerning documents, exhibits, and
               names of witnesses to be called during the hearing. Such information shall be exchanged
               not less than five business days prior to the hearing. Upon motion by either party,
               the hearing officer shall be authorized to compel such exchange of information.
(b)
If the hearing officer determines that a party has failed to exchange information
               in good faith, the hearing officer may exclude documents, exhibits, and witnesses
               whose names have not been previously made available to the other party, if such evidence
               would constitute an unfair surprise. In the absence of bad faith, the hearing officer
               may require that previously undisclosed information be turned over to the other party
               and may continue the hearing for such time as may reasonably be needed for review
               of the previously undisclosed evidence.
(c)
Only those witnesses, documents, and exhibits to be used in the hearing may be compelled
               by the hearing officer. Nothing in this section shall confer upon the hearing officer
               the power to compel production of documents or files of a protected or privileged
               nature, nor to compel either party to create documents or conduct research for or
               on behalf of the other party, or to compel production of documents or witnesses not
               presented or called at the hearing.
(Code 1981, § 2-147; Ord. No. 3608, §§ 1, 2, 4-3-2003)
